Registry:   stage -> production with the metrics attached (MLflow registry)
Serving:    REST/gRPC endpoint, or batch job; pin model version, canary 5%
Monitor:    data drift (input distribution shifted), concept drift
            (input->output relation shifted), latency, cost
Retrain:    scheduled or drift-triggered, never silently online-learning

Drift alarms you actually need:
  - input distribution PSI/KL over threshold
  - proxy metric in production (e.g. click-through) dropping vs holdout
  - latency p95 and error rate of the endpoint

8. Learning vs Production

AspectWhile learningIn production
DataTitanic.csv from a tutorialPipeline with validation, PII handling, versioned snapshots
EvaluationAccuracy on one splitRight metric for the cost, cross-validated, business KPI A/B tested
ModelBest notebook scoreVersioned, reproducible, with model card and owner
Servingpredict() in the notebookBatched endpoint, timeout, fallback to rules, load tested
After launchDoneDrift monitoring, alerting, retraining policy, rollback to last good

9. Key Takeaways

  • ML inverts programming: data + answers -> rules, driven by a loss function and an optimiser.
  • Train/val/test discipline and leakage checks matter more than model choice.
  • XGBoost wins tabular; neural nets win perceptual data (images, speech, text).
  • Pick the metric from the cost of mistakes before training.
  • Backprop + gradient descent is one four-line ritual repeated everywhere.
  • Production ML is mostly data pipelines and monitoring, not modelling.

Exercise: take any CSV with a binary label, run train/test split, fit logistic regression and random forest, print both classification reports, and explain in one sentence why the better F1 one can still be the wrong model for the business.

chapters.title: AI Models
chapters.html:
1. The One Idea Behind Modern AI: Tokens And Prediction

Every large language model is doing one thing: given a sequence of tokens, predict the next token - a probability distribution over the whole vocabulary. Chat is sampling from that distribution billions of times.

Your text  -> tokenizer  -> [5023, 891, 17, 4471, ...]  -> model  -> P(next token)
                              "The cat sat on the"              sample -> " mat"

BPE tokenizer: merges frequent character pairs into tokens, so vocabulary
is ~50k words/pieces - unknown words are spelled from subwords.
Context window: how many tokens the model can attend to at once
  (4k -> 128k -> 1M). Everything beyond it is invisible to the model.

2. The Transformer And Self-Attention

Attention answers: for each token, which other tokens matter most right now? Every token emits a Query (what I seek), a Key (what I offer), and a Value (what I will pass on).

Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax( Q * K^T / sqrt(d_k) ) * V

"The bank raised the river bank"
 token "bank" #2 attends strongly to "river" - context resolves meaning

Multi-head: several attention patterns in parallel (syntax here, coreference
there), concatenated and projected. Stack N of these blocks (GPT: 96+)
with feed-forward layers between them - that is a transformer.

Why it beat RNNs: full parallelism in training (GPU friendly) and direct
long-range connections - token 1 can influence token 4000 in one step.

3. How A Model Gets Smart: Training Stages

StageWhat happensDataCost
PretrainingNext-token prediction on the internetTens of TB of textThousands of GPUs, millions of dollars
SFT (fine-tuning)Learn to follow instructions / chat format~10k-1M high-quality Q&ADozens of GPUs
RLHF / DPOAlign with human preference: helpful, harmless, honestPreference rankingsReinforcement loop
QuantisationShrink weights (fp16 -> int8 -> int4)Same modelCheap - enables local running
DistillationTrain a small model to mimic a big oneBig-model outputsModerate
LoRA / QLoRATrain small adapter matrices, freeze the baseYour dataset1 GPU feasible

4. The Model Families

FamilyHow it worksRepresentativesUse for
Decoder-only LLMPredict next token, bidirectional-free (causal)GPT-4/4o, Llama 3, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeekChat, code, agents, RAG
Encoder-onlyBidirectional understanding, no generationBERT, RoBERTa, DeBERTaClassification, search ranking, NER
Encoder-decoderRead whole input, then generate outputT5, BART, Flan-T5Translation, summarisation
MultimodalAttention over images + text (+audio) togetherGPT-4o, Gemini, Claude 3.x, LLaVAVision QA, document understanding
DiffusionIteratively denoise random pixels into an imageStable Diffusion, DALL-E, MidjourneyImage generation/editing
SpeechSpectrograms -> text and backWhisper, ElevenLabsTranscription, TTS
Embedding modelsText -> vector, cosine similarity = meaningOpenAI text-embedding-3, bge, e5, CohereRAG, search, clustering
RerankersScore query-document pairs preciselyCohere rerank, bge-rerankerImprove RAG retrieval top-k
Small / on-deviceQuantised, runs locallyLlama 3.2 3B, Phi-3, Gemma 2B, GPT-OSS-miniOffline, cheap, private

5. Vision And Sequence Models Before Transformers

ModelMechanismWhere it still lives
CNNConvolution kernels detect edges/textures then shapesImage classification, medical imaging, real-time vision
RNN / LSTM / GRUHidden state walks the sequence step by stepLegacy time-series; replaced by Transformers
Autoencoder / VAECompress then reconstruct; sample the latent spaceAnomaly detection, compression
GANGenerator fools a discriminatorOlder image synthesis, data augmentation
Tree modelsGradient-boosted decision treesTabular data - still usually unbeaten

6. Inference: What You Pay For

latency  = queue + prefill (processing your prompt) + decode (tokens out)
cost     = input tokens * rate_in  +  output tokens * rate_out
           (output tokens are usually 3-4x the price - be terse)
context  = prompt + history + retrieved docs; all billed every call

Levers:
  - trim history / summarise old turns
  - smaller model for easy steps, big model for hard steps (routing)
  - cache: prompt caching (OpenAI/Anthropic) and semantic caching
  - stream tokens so the user sees first bytes instantly (TTFB)
  - batch non-urgent calls (batch APIs are ~50% cheaper)
  - temperature: 0 for extraction/code, 0.7+ for brainstorming

Memory trick: models do not "look things up" - they regurgitate patterns from training. That is why they hallucinate citations and why RAG (Chapter 41) exists: put real documents in the context and make the model quote them.

7. Choosing A Model In Practice

Need                         Look at
-----                        --------
Just starting / cheap        GPT-4o-mini class or Llama 3.1 8B local
Hard reasoning / code        Frontier: GPT-4.1/5 class, Claude Opus/Sonnet,
                             Gemini Pro - benchmark on YOUR tasks
Fully private / offline       Llama/Qwen/Gemma 3-14B quantised via ollama
Vision + text                GPT-4o, Gemini, Claude
RAG retrieval                Dedicated embedding model + reranker
Classification at scale      Fine-tuned small encoder (BERT) - beats LLMs
                             on cost and latency
Speech                       Whisper large-v3 (ASR), TTS vendor or Piper

Evaluation beats vibes: build a 50-200 case eval set from your real
questions, run every candidate model through it, compare accuracy AND cost
AND latency.

8. Learning vs Production

AspectWhile learningIn production
Where it runsChat UI in a browserAPI from your backend, keys in a secret manager, no client-side keys
PromptSame chat window, hand-typedVersioned templates, evals in CI, A/B on prompts
HallucinationFun anecdoteRAG + citation checks + refusal policy + human review for high stakes
CostFree tierBudgets, per-feature cost tracking, cache and route
DataPaste anythingPII redaction, retention policy, regional endpoints

9. Key Takeaways

  • LLMs predict the next token with attention - everything else is training stages and sampling settings.
  • Pretrain -> SFT -> RLHF -> quantise: where the capability and the cost come from.
  • Decoder-only for generation, encoder-only for classification, enc-dec for transduction; diffusion for images.
  • Context window, latency, price per 1M tokens - the three numbers to check before choosing a model.
  • Benchmark on YOUR eval set; vibes are not evaluation.
  • Models generate plausible text - ground them with RAG before trusting their facts.

Exercise: take five real questions from your domain, run them through two different models at temperature 0, and build a tiny eval sheet - accuracy, latency, cost per answer. That sheet is your model selection process.

chapters.title: AI Engineering and RAG
chapters.html:
1. Prompt Engineering Is Software Design

TechniqueWhat it isExample
Role (system prompt)Fixes persona, scope and rules for every callYou are a support assistant for DocKube. Only answer from the provided context.
Structured outputSchema the reply must obey (JSON mode / tool call){"verdict": ..., "confidence": ..., "evidence": [...]}
Few-shot2-5 worked examples = fastest quality boostInput -> perfect output, repeated in the prompt
Step-by-stepAsk for reasoning before the answer for hard problemsThink through it, then output only the final JSON
ConstraintsExplicit don\'ts and limits beat vibesMax 3 bullets. Never invent citations. If unsure, say "not in context".
SeparationInstructions vs data in distinct blocks<<CONTEXT>> ... <</CONTEXT>> then the question
SYSTEM: You extract invoices. Rules: return JSON only, no markdown,
missing field = null, dates ISO-8601. If the document is not an invoice,
return {"error": "not_an_invoice"}.

USER: Extract from this text: "Invoice #8841, 3 Jan 2026, ACME Ltd, total 420.00"

# Version your prompts like code: prompts/invoice_v3.md in git, eval suite
# runs on every change (see section 5). Prompt changes ARE releases.

2. Function Calling And Tool Use

import json, httpx
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()
TOOLS = [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
        "name": "get_order_status",
        "description": "Look up a customer order by id",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"order_id": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["order_id"],
        },
    },
}]

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=messages, tools=TOOLS, temperature=0)
msg = resp.choices[0].message
if msg.tool_calls:                       # the model ASKS you to run something
    for call in msg.tool_calls:
        args = json.loads(call.function.arguments)
        result = orders_api(args["order_id"])   # YOUR code does the real work
        messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id,
                         "content": json.dumps(result)})
    # feed results back - the model writes the natural-language answer

Memory trick: the model never touches your system - it calls tools and your code executes them. That boundary is where you put auth, validation and rate limits.

3. RAG - Retrieval Augmented Generation

LLMs do not know your docs, your policies, or last week's changes. RAG retrieves the relevant passages and puts them in the prompt, so answers are grounded and citable.

INGEST (offline)                          QUERY (online)
1. load documents (pdf, md, html, tickets)
2. chunk: 300-800 tokens, 10-20% overlap
   (respect headings; never split mid-table)
3. embed each chunk -> vector            1. embed the question
4. store {vector, text, source, meta}    2. top-k similarity search (k=5..20)
   in a vector DB                        3. optional reranker on top 20 -> top 5
                                          4. build prompt: context + question
                                          5. generate with citations
                                          6. return answer + sources

# Full minimal RAG in Python (pip install openai chromadb tiktoken)
from openai import OpenAI
import chromadb

client = OpenAI()
DB = chromadb.PersistentClient(path="./vector_store")
col = DB.get_or_create_collection("docs", metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"})

def chunks_of(path: str, size: int = 700, overlap: int = 100):
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    return [text[i:i + size] for i in range(0, len(text), size - overlap)]

def ingest(path: str):
    for n, chunk in enumerate(chunks_of(path)):
        vec = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embedding-3-small",
                                       input=chunk).data[0].embedding
        col.add(ids=[f"{path}#{n}"], embeddings=[vec],
                documents=[chunk], metadatas=[{"source": path, "chunk": n}])

def rag(question: str, k: int = 6) -> dict:
    qvec = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embedding-3-small",
                                    input=question).data[0].embedding
    hits = col.query(query_embeddings=[qvec], n_results=k)
    context = "\n\n---\n\n".join(hits["documents"][0])
    sources = [m["source"] for m in hits["metadatas"][0]]

    out = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0,
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content":
             "Answer ONLY from the context. Quote the source filename after "
             "each claim. If the context does not cover it, say "
             "'not in context'."},
            {"role": "user", "content": f"CONTEXT:\n{context}\n\nQ: {question}"},
        ])
    return {"answer": out.choices[0].message.content,
            "sources": sorted(set(sources))}
Vector DBShapeChoose when
Chroma / FAISSEmbedded libraryLocal, single app, millions of vectors
pgvectorPostgres extensionYou already run Postgres - one system less
Qdrant / MilvusVector serverLarge scale, filters, hybrid search
Pinecone / Weaviate cloudManagedNo ops budget
Elasticsearch / OpenSearchKeyword + vector hybridYou need BM25 AND semantic together

Retrieval quality beats model quality. Fix in this order: better chunking (headers, semantic), hybrid search (keyword + vector), reranker, metadata filters, query rewriting - then worry about the LLM.

4. Agents - Models With A Loop

plan  -> choose tool  -> execute  -> observe result  -> repeat until done

Rules that keep agents alive in production:
- max iterations (10) and a hard timeout - loops cost money
- every tool validated server-side (the model can pass ANY argument)
- idempotent tools: retries will happen
- keep a full trace of every step for debugging and billing
- prefer deterministic workflows; use agents only where steps cannot be known

5. Evals - The Test Suite For LLM Features

Three layers, cheapest first:
1. PROMPT regression set   50-200 real cases with expected properties
   - deterministic (temperature 0), runs in CI on every prompt/model change
2. RAG retrieval metrics   hit@k, MRR, context precision - did the right
   chunks even reach the prompt?
3. LLM-as-judge            a big model scores style/consistency on a rubric
   (cheap for tone; never the sole judge of correctness)

# A tiny eval harness
import json, statistics

def run_eval(cases, prompt_fn, model="gpt-4o-mini"):
    rows = []
    for case in cases:
        got = prompt_fn(case["input"])             # temperature=0
        rows.append({
            "id": case["id"],
            "exact":  got.strip() == case["expected"].strip(),
            "contains": case["must_contain"].lower() in got.lower(),
            "output": got,
        })
    score = sum(r["exact"] or r["contains"] for r in rows) / len(rows)
    return score, rows                             # gate merges at e.g. >= 0.9

# Regression case format:
{"id": "refund-3", "input": "Can I refund order 77?",
 "expected": "Refunds allowed within 30 days", "must_contain": "30 days"}
Failure modeEval catches itFix
Answer changed after prompt editRegression set score dropsRevert or update cases deliberately
Wrong chunks retrievedhit@k fallsChunking, hybrid search, rerank
Format drift (markdown in JSON)Schema validation failsStructured outputs / tool calls
Hallucinated factsCitation checks + judgeStricter grounding prompt, refuse policy
Cost or latency regressionToken/latency dashboardsShorter prompts, caching, routing

6. Guardrails, Safety And Privacy

Input side (before the model):
  - PII detection + redaction (names, cards, emails) before any external API
  - prompt-injection scan: user text is DATA, never instructions
    ("ignore previous instructions" must be neutralised by system-prompt
     separation + tool allow-lists)
  - allow-listed topics; jailbreak pattern matching

Output side (after the model):
  - schema validation (JSON, enums, lengths)
  - citation check: every claim must map to a retrieved chunk
  - toxicity / secret scanning (the model may echo training data)
  - never render model output as HTML/JS unescaped; never let it issue
    privileged actions without an approval step

Operational:
  - rate limits per user, budget caps per feature, kill switch
  - log inputs/outputs with retention limits; audit trail for tool calls
  - content policy + a human review queue for high-risk categories

Memory trick: the model is the least trustworthy component in the pipeline - validate everything that crosses its mouth, and validate everything that enters it.

7. Fine-Tune Or RAG Or Prompt? Decide In This Order

SituationRight toolWhy
Model lacks a format or personaPrompt + few-shotMinutes of work, no data needed
Model lacks YOUR factsRAGGrounded, citable, updates without retraining
Model is right but slow/priceyDistil/route: small model for easy casesCheapest lever is usually routing
Model must output a strict style/schema at scaleFine-tune (SFT/LoRA)Shorter prompts, consistent format, cheaper inference
Domain jargon, classification, code styleFine-tune small model100s-1000s of examples beat a big general model
Need knowledge freshnessRAG over the source, never fine-tune for factsFine-tuning bakes facts in untraceably

8. Shipping LLM Apps In FastAPI

# app/routers/ai.py - streaming RAG endpoint
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
import json, asyncio

router = APIRouter(prefix="/ai", tags=["ai"])

@router.post("/ask")
async def ask(body: AskIn, user = Depends(get_current_user),
              svc = Depends(get_rag_service)):
    await enforce_quota(user["sub"], cost=body)
    sources = await svc.retrieve(body.question, k=6)
    if not sources:
        return {"answer": "not in context", "sources": []}

    async def stream():
        # Server-Sent Events: first token in <500ms, tokens as they arrive
        stream = await svc.client.chat.completions.create(
            model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0, stream=True,
            messages=build_messages(body.question, sources))
        async for event in stream:
            delta = event.choices[0].delta.content or ""
            yield f"data: {json.dumps({'t': delta})}\n\n"
        yield f"data: {json.dumps({'sources': [s.source for s in sources]})}\n\n"

    return StreamingResponse(stream(), media_type="text/event-stream")

# Also wire: request-id middleware, per-user token budget in Redis,
# timeouts on the provider call, and a circuit breaker so a provider
# outage degrades to "classical search results" instead of a 500.

# What production LLM ops monitors (LLMOps):
metric                 alert when
-----                  ----------
p50/p95 latency        p95 > 2s for streaming first token
tokens per request     +30% vs baseline (prompt bloat or injection)
cost per feature/day   budget burn rate
eval score             < gate on each deploy (prompts ship like code)
refusal / no-answer %  rising = retrieval or policy broke
tool error rate        tool schema drift or upstream failure
groundedness (judge)   claims without supporting chunks

9. Learning vs Production

AspectWhile learningIn production
PromptTyped fresh in the playgroundVersioned file, eval-gated, feature-flagged
ContextPaste the doc in by handIngestion pipeline, chunk versioning, retrieval metrics
API keyIn the scriptSecret manager, per-service keys, spend limits
OutputPrinted and trustedSchema-validated, citation-checked, rate-limited, logged
FailureException in the notebookTimeout + fallback + circuit breaker + user-visible degraded mode
DataAnything goesRedaction, retention limits, regional endpoints, DPA with provider

10. Key Takeaways

  • Prompt = code: version it, test it, ship it behind flags.
  • Function calling is a boundary: the model proposes, your code disposes (auth, validation, idempotency live on your side).
  • RAG grounds answers: chunk carefully, hybrid search + rerank, cite everything; retrieval quality beats model choice.
  • Agents need iteration limits, validated tools and full traces - prefer deterministic workflows where steps are known.
  • Eval sets in CI are the only thing that makes LLM changes safe.
  • Guardrails on both sides of the model; the model is untrusted in both directions.

Exercise: build the ingest + query RAG pair from section 3 over five of your own documents, then break retrieval on purpose (wrong chunk size) and watch the eval score drop before you touch the model.

chapters.title: Platform Engineering
chapters.html:
1. Why Platform Engineering Exists

Every DevOps team eventually hits the same wall: twenty product teams each assembling the same pipeline, the same Kubernetes boilerplate, the same dashboards - badly. Platform engineering is the answer: a dedicated team builds one internal platform so product teams ship features instead of plumbing.

Old world (DevOps at scale)Platform world
Every team owns its toolchain; expertise is unevenOne paved road, maintained by specialists
Ticket ops: file a ticket, wait three daysSelf-service with guardrails: click, get a database
Config sprawl, every repo differentGolden paths: templates that encode the standards
Cognitive load on every developerDevelopers think about the product, not the platform
Platform is a side duty nobody ownsPlatform is a product with users, SLAs and a roadmap

Memory trick: DevOps changed how teams work; platform engineering changes what each team has to know. The product of a platform team is a paved road, and adoption - not uptime - is its real metric.

2. The Internal Developer Platform, Down To The Atom

An IDP is the golden path made clickable. Every atom a service needs:

LayerThe platform providesUnder the hood
Compute"New service" button -> deployed workloadK8s namespace / VM / serverless, autoscaling, rollout policy
NetworkingHostname, ingress, service discovery, mTLSGateway, DNS record, cert-manager, mesh policy
StorageVolume / bucket self-servicePVC templates, S3 buckets with lifecycle rules
DatabasesProvisioned DB with backups onOperator (CloudNativePG, Postgres operator), PITR, credentials injected
SecretsTeam secrets store, automatic injectionVault / AWS SM, short-lived leases, no secret in git
CI/CDBuild, test, sign, deploy from one fileGitHub Actions/Tekton, supply chain (cosign, SBOM), progressive delivery
EnvironmentsPreview / staging / prod from templatesEphemeral preview envs per PR, prod behind approvals
ObservabilityDashboards, logs, traces, alerts auto-wiredOpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, on-call rotation defaults
PolicyGuardrails you cannot turn offOPA/Gatekeeper: no privileged pods, images from approved registries
FinOpsCost per team, per serviceLabels, showback dashboards, budget alerts

3. Internal Developer Portal - The Catalog

The internal developer portal (Backstage is the reference implementation) is the UI over all of it: a live catalog of every service, its owner, its docs, its scorecards, and a button to scaffold a new one.

Software catalog (the core object model)
  Component   - a service, a library, a website
  API         - contracts components expose
  System      - grouping of components delivering one capability
  Resource    - DB, bucket, topic a component consumes
  User/Team   - owners; every entity HAS an owner

Every entity gets: description, owner, tags, links, on-call, docs,
dashboards, scorecards - generated when scaffolded, kept live from CI.

Scaffolder template (golden path as code):
  1. developer clicks "New Node service"
  2. template fills repo: FastAPI structure, Dockerfile, CI, OTel, alerts
  3. registers it in the catalog with owner = your team
  4. provisions staging DB + secrets, wires dashboards
  5. first deploy -> production behind the standard progressive rollout
Scorecard (examples)Gate
Has owner + on-call rotationRequired to graduate to prod
SLO defined, error budget visibleBlocks high-risk changes when burned
CI runs tests + SAST + dependency scanBranch protection requires it
Runs the golden-path base imageNon-compliant = tracked debt with a deadline
Deploys via standard pipelineNo ad-hoc kubectl to prod, ever

4. Golden Paths, Templates And Self-Service

Golden path = the easiest way to do the right thing, and a visible door
for every other way (with friction, review, and a recorded exception).

Not: "you MUST use our JVM library" (platform as bureaucracy)
Yes: "new service? 15 minutes, secure defaults, zero tickets" - and if you
     deviate, you own the tests, dashboards and security review for it.

Scaffold sources of truth:
  repo templates (Cookiecutter, create-*)  -> code lives in git
  Helm/Jsonnet/Kustomize overlays           -> infra lives in git
  Crossplane / Terraform modules            -> cloud resources as code
  API-first IDP                             -> everything callable, everything audited

5. The Team Topology View

TeamResponsibilityInterfaces
Platform teamThe paved road: IDP, pipelines, runtime, DBs, observabilitySelf-service APIs + docs + office hours
Enabling teamCoaches stuck product teams onto the platformTemporary pairing, playbooks
Stream-aligned (product) teamsBusiness value, own services end to endPlatform golden paths
Enabling vs X-as-a-ServiceXaaS publishes consumable capabilities; enabling teaches-

Thinnest viable platform: start with ONE golden path (build + deploy + database) that a single team loves, publish it, measure adoption, then expand. A platform nobody adopts is expensive shelfware. Anti-pattern to watch: the platform team blocking product teams with reviews - guardrails should be automatic, not human queues.

6. GitOps - The Platform\'s Control Loop

git push (desired state)
   -> Flux / Argo CD watches the repo
   -> diffs live cluster vs git
   -> applies changes, reports status back
   -> drift? cluster is RECONCILED back to git automatically

Why it matters for platforms:
  - self-service = open a PR; approval is code review
  - every change auditable, revertible (git revert), and reviewable
  - cluster credentials stay with the controller, not with developers
  - multi-cluster: one repo, many overlays (staging, prod, regions)

7. Emerging Tech Around The Platform

TrendWhat it isWhy it matters now
Platform engineeringIDPs and golden pathsCognitive load is the bottleneck at scale
AI-assisted ops (AIOps + copilots)LLMs reading logs/alerts, suggesting fixes, writing pipelinesReduces MTTR; keep a human on the approve button
WebAssembly (WASM) at the edge/serverSandboxed near-native componentsPlugin systems, edge functions, safer untrusted code
Edge computingCompute near the user (CDN functions, IoT gateways)Latency-sensitive features without central round-trips
FinOps engineeringCost as an engineering metric in the platformUnit economics per feature, showback drives behaviour
Supply-chain securitySLSA, SBOM, cosign signing, provenanceAttacks moved upstream to build systems
Confidential computingEncrypted memory enclaves (SEV/TDX)Compliance for regulated workloads in the cloud
Sustainable/green computingCarbon-aware scheduling, efficiency metricsCost and compliance are converging

8. Learning vs Production

AspectWhile learningIn production
PlatformOne laptop running minikube + a MakefileMulti-tenant IDP with quotas, quotas per team, SSO, audit
ProvisioningTicket or click in a consoleSelf-service API, policy-gated, costed, auto-decommissioned if idle
StandardsREADME adviceScorecards enforced at the pipeline with escape hatches
Adoption-Measured: % services on golden path, lead time, onboarding time
SupportAsk the one person who built itDocs, office hours, SLO for the platform itself

9. Key Takeaways

  • Platform engineering = product thinking applied to internal tooling: users, adoption metrics, paved roads.
  • The IDP covers compute, network, storage, databases, secrets, CI/CD, observability, policy and cost - self-service with the guardrails built in.
  • The catalog (Backstage) makes ownership and standards visible; scorecards make them enforceable.
  • GitOps turns every change into a reviewed, revertible commit and fixes drift automatically.
  • Start with the thinnest viable platform; adoption is the only metric that counts at first.
  • AI, WASM, edge and supply-chain security are the next waves landing ON the platform - which is exactly why the platform exists.

Exercise: draw your dream IDP as a catalog: list every atom a new service needs (from the table in section 2), mark which are tickets today, and sketch the one golden path that would remove the most tickets.

chapters.title: Docker Deep Dive
chapters.html:
1. The Mental Model

Registry (Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR)   store of IMAGES
   image  = immutable template: OS libs + app + config, layered
   container = RUNNING instance of an image (writable layer on top)
   Dockerfile = build instructions for an image
   volume = data that outlives the container
   network = private bridge so containers can find each other

   Dockerfile --docker build--> IMAGE --docker run--> CONTAINER
                                      ^                  |
                                      +--docker commit---+  (discouraged)
ConceptRule of thumb
LayersEach instruction = one cached layer; order matters - put rarely changing steps (deps) before frequently changing (source)
ContainerOne concern per container; stateless by default; stoppable and replaceable
Image tag vs digestTags move (latest lies); pin :sha256-... in production
Writable layerEverything written to the container rootfs dies with it - use volumes

2. Daemon, Contexts And Info

docker version                      # client + server versions
 docker info                        # storage driver, runtime, registry mirrors, containers
 docker context ls                  # local vs remote daemons
docker context use remote-prod      # point the CLI at another daemon
docker system df                    # space used by images, containers, volumes
 docker system df -v                # per-image layer breakdown + who uses what
 DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build .   # BuildKit (default since 23.x)
docker context inspect
systemctl status docker             # Linux daemon
Get-Service docker                  # Windows
journalctl -u docker -e            # daemon log

3. Running Containers - The run Flag Encyclopedia

# The flags you will use every day
docker run -d --name web -p 8080:80 --restart unless-stopped nginx:1.27
           ^   ^        ^        ^          ^
     detached  name  host:container  restart policy

# Full catalogue
docker run -it --rm ubuntu:24.04 bash        # interactive shell, delete on exit
docker run -d -e API_KEY=abc -e MODE=prod myapp            # environment vars
docker run -d --env-file .env myapp                        # env from file
docker run -d -v /host/data:/var/data myapp                # bind mount
docker run -d -v dbdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data postgres   # named volume
docker run -d --mount type=bind,src=/h,dst=/r,readonly myapp
docker run --network app-net --add-host db:10.0.0.5 myapp  # custom DNS entry
docker run -d --memory 512m --cpus 1.5 myapp               # hard limits
docker run -d --read-only --tmpfs /tmp myapp               # immutable rootfs
docker run --user 1000:1000 myapp                          # non-root
docker run -d --health-cmd "curl -f localhost/" --health-interval 30s myapp
docker run -d --log-driver json-file --log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3 myapp
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 postgres                  # localhost only
docker run -d --pull always myapp                          # never trust local tag

# Lifecycle (equivalents in order)
docker create --name x myapp        # allocated, not started
docker start x | stop x | restart x
 docker pause x / unpause x         # freeze the cgroup (SIGSTOP)
docker kill x                       # SIGKILL
 docker rm x                         # remove stopped container
 docker rm -f x                      # force remove
 docker rename old new
docker wait x                       # block until it exits (exit code)
docker update --memory 1g x         # resize a running container

4. Inspecting And Debugging Running Containers

docker ps                 # running;  docker ps -a  # all (incl. exited)
docker ps -q --filter status=exited            # just the dead ones
docker ps --filter name=web --format "table {{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}\t{{.Ports}}"

docker logs -f --tail 100 --since 10m web      # follow with context
 docker logs -f --timestamps web 2>&1 | grep -i error

docker exec -it web sh                        # shell (sh exists everywhere)
docker exec -it web bash                      # bash if the image has it
docker exec -u root web id                    # who am I, which uid
docker exec web env                           # environment actually set
docker exec web cat /etc/resolv.conf          # DNS the container sees

 docker inspect web                           # everything: IPs, mounts, env, health
 docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' web
docker inspect -f '{{json .State.Health}}' web | python -m json.tool
 docker top web                               # host processes inside it
docker stats                                  # live CPU/mem/net (all containers)
 docker stats --no-stream --format "table {{.Name}}\t{{.CPUPerc}}\t{{.MemUsage}}"

docker diff web                               # what changed in the filesystem
 docker port web                              # port mappings
docker cp web:/var/log/app.log ./local.log    # copy out
 docker cp ./fixture.json web:/tmp/           # copy in
 docker export web -o snapshot.tar            # filesystem snapshot (no history)
FieldWhere it lives
Entrypoint / Cmddocker inspect web -> Config.Entrypoint / Config.Cmd
Exit codeState.ExitCode - the number your restart loop is hiding
HealthState.Health.Status: starting / healthy / unhealthy
MountsMounts[] - Source, Destination, RW
Logs driverHostConfig.LogConfig

5. Building Images

docker build -t myapp:1.0 .                    # from Dockerfile in cwd
docker build --no-cache -t myapp:1.0 .         # ignore cache (flaky builds)
docker build --pull -t myapp:1.0 .             # fresh base image
docker build -f Dockerfile.prod -t myapp:prod .
docker build --target dev -t myapp:dev .       # multi-stage: stop at a stage
docker build --build-arg VERSION=1.2 -t myapp .
docker build -t myapp . && docker image prune -f  # remove dangling after build

# BuildKit extras (faster, more powerful)
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 -t myapp:1.0 --push .
docker buildx ls                              # builders and their platforms
docker buildx build --push --cache-from type=gha --cache-to type=gha,mode=max .
# Cache mounts survive across builds (huge for apt/pip):
#   RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt apt-get install -y build-essential

# The Dockerfile that production deserves
FROM python:3.12-slim AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .

FROM python:3.12-slim
RUN useradd -r appuser
WORKDIR /srv
COPY --from=build /usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages /usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages
COPY --from=build /app .
USER appuser
EXPOSE 8000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s CMD python -c "import urllib.request;urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8000/health')"
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0"]
InstructionPurposeTip
FROMBase imagePin minor version, prefer slim/distroless
COPY / ADDFiles in (ADD also handles URLs/tar - prefer COPY)COPY requirements first for cache
RUNExecute at buildCombine with &&, clean apt lists in the same layer
ENV / ARGENV baked into image, ARG build-onlyNever ARG a secret - it leaks into layers
EXPOSEDocumentation only-p still required at run time
CMD / ENTRYPOINTCMD = default args (overridable), ENTRYPOINT = the executableENTRYPOINT ["app"] + CMD ["--port","80"] is the combo
WORKDIRcd for everything afterAbsolute path; never cd in a RUN then forget
USERRun as non-rootSecurity baseline - always set it
VOLUMEDeclare a mount pointAnonymous volumes leak - name them
HEALTHCHECKContainer health probeDocker restarts nothing; orchestration acts on it
.dockerignoreExclude .git, venv, node_modules, secrets from contextCuts build time and accidental secret leaks
docker history myapp:1.0                       # layer sizes - find the bloat
docker image inspect myapp:1.0 --format '{{json .Config.Env}}'
docker image save myapp:1.0 -o myapp.tar       # offline transfer
docker image load -i myapp.tar
docker image tag myapp:1.0 registry.example.com/team/myapp:1.0
docker image rm myapp:1.0                      # fails if a container uses it
docker image prune                             # dangling images only
docker image prune -a                          # EVERY unused image (careful)
docker search nginx                            # hub search (rarely useful)
docker pull nginx@sha256:ab...                 # digest-pinned pull

6. Networks

docker network ls
docker network create app-net                  # bridge (the default kind)
docker network create --driver bridge --subnet 10.10.0.0/24 --gateway 10.10.0.1 net1
docker network inspect app-net                 # containers + IPs + options

docker run -d --name api --network app-net myapi
docker run -d --name db  --network app-net postgres
docker network connect app-net legacy          # attach a running container
docker network disconnect app-net legacy
docker network rm app-net && docker network prune -f

# Containers on the same user-defined network resolve each other BY NAME:
psql -h db -U app        # "db" is the container name - built-in DNS
DriverScopeUse for
bridge (default)HostContainers on one host talking by name
hostHostNo isolation - max performance, no port mapping
none-Air-gapped jobs
overlayClusterSwarm services across hosts
macvlanHostContainer gets its own MAC on the physical LAN
custom (CNI/Calico)ClusterKubernetes - Docker\'s network is bypassed there

Memory trick: the default bridge does NOT do name resolution - user-defined networks do. If "cannot connect to mysql", first question: same user-defined network?

7. Volumes And Data

docker volume ls
docker volume create --driver local --opt type=nfs --opt o=addr=10.0.0.5 --opt device=/shares/data nfs-data
docker run -d -v pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data --name db postgres
docker volume inspect pgdata                    # find the real host path
 docker volume rm pgdata                        # fails while in use
 docker volume prune -f                         # ALL unused volumes - data loss if wrong

# Back up a volume the right way (stop writer first, or use pg_dump)
docker run --rm -v pgdata:/data -v $(pwd):/backup alpine \
  tar czf /backup/pgdata-$(date +%F).tar.gz -C /data .

# Bind mount vs named volume
bind mount:  -v /host/path:/container/path     host path, absolute, host FS semantics
named volume: -v name:/container/path          Docker-managed, portable, backup-able
read-only:    -v name:/path:ro

8. Registries, Login And Distribution

docker login                                  # Docker Hub (or docker login ghcr.io)
docker login registry.example.com -u ci --password-stdin   # CI: never on the argv
docker logout --all
docker pull nginx:1.27
 docker push registry.example.com/team/app:1.27
docker search --limit 10 flask
docker tag app:1.27 myname/app:latest          # retag before push
 docker manifest inspect nginx:1.27            # what platforms does it have?

# Version discipline:
#   :1.27        immutable release tag
#   :1.27-alpine variant
#   :latest       convenience ONLY on your laptop
#   @sha256:...  what production deploys

# Private registry in a pinch:
docker run -d -p 5000:5000 --name registry -v regdata:/var/lib/registry registry:2
docker tag app:1.0 localhost:5000/app:1.0 && docker push localhost:5000/app:1.0

9. Docker Compose - Multi-Container In One File

docker compose up -d                           # create + start detached
docker compose up -d --build                   # rebuild changed images first
docker compose up -d --force-recreate          # recreate from scratch
docker compose ps                              # status of this project
docker compose logs -f --tail 100 api          # follow one service
docker compose exec db psql -U app             # shell/command in a service
docker compose run --rm web pytest             # one-off task (no deps sharing)
docker compose restart api
 docker compose stop web / start web
 docker compose pause api / unpause api
docker compose pull && docker compose build --no-cache
docker compose config                          # rendered, validated YAML (secrets resolved)
docker compose top                             # processes per service
docker compose down                            # stop + remove containers + network
docker compose down -v                         # ALSO deletes volumes - DATA LOSS
docker compose down --rmi all --volumes         # nuclear cleanup
docker compose -f base.yml -f prod.yml up -d   # layered files
COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=shop docker compose up -d # isolate parallel copies

# docker-compose.yml reference (Compose specification)
services:
  web:
    build: .                          # or image: ghcr.io/me/web:1.0
    ports: ["8080:80"]
    environment: {NODE_ENV: production}
    env_file: [.env]
    depends_on:                       # startup ORDER + health gating
      db: {condition: service_healthy}
    volumes: ["./src:/app:ro"]
    networks: [frontend]
    deploy:                           # swarm/stack semantics
      replicas: 2
      resources: {limits: {cpus: "0.50", memory: 512M}}
      restart_policy: {condition: on-failure}
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost/health"]
      interval: 30s
      retries: 3
    restart: unless-stopped

  db:
    image: postgres:16
    volumes: [pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:?set DB_PASSWORD}   # fail fast if unset

volumes:
  pgdata:
networks:
  frontend:
GotchaFix
depends_on does not wait for readinesscondition: service_healthy + a healthcheck
Secrets in environmentCompose secrets / env_file outside git; never in the image
Stale images after branch switchcompose up -d --build, or --pull always
Two checkouts collide on portsCOMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME or different host ports

10. Swarm - Built-In Orchestration

docker swarm init                               # manager token printed
docker swarm join --token SWARM-WORKER ...      # run on workers
docker node ls                                  # membership and status

docker service create --name web --replicas 3 --publish 80:80 myapp:1.0
docker service ls / docker service ps web
 docker service scale web=5
docker service update --image myapp:1.1 web     # rolling update
docker service logs web
docker stack deploy -c compose.yml shop         # compose-driven swarm
docker stack ls / services / docker stack rm shop

# Swarm vs Kubernetes: Swarm is batteries-included and simple; Kubernetes
# won the ecosystem (operators, autoscalers, ecosystem). Learn Swarm to
# understand the concepts cheaply, invest in Kubernetes for production.

11. System And Cleanup

docker system df
 docker system df -v
 docker system events --since 10m               # live daemon activity stream
docker system prune                             # stopped containers + dangling images + unused networks
docker system prune -a --volumes                # EVERYTHING unused - read df first!
docker container prune -f                       # stopped containers only
docker image prune -a -f                        # all unused images
docker network prune -f                         # unused networks
 docker volume prune -f                          # unused volumes (DATA)
docker builder prune -a -f                      # build cache (speeds vs space)
docker trust inspect myapp:1.0                  # content trust signatures

Memory trick: cleanup order of safety: container prune -> image prune -f -> builder prune -> network prune -> volume prune LAST and never with -a on a host you do not know. system df -v before ANY prune.

12. Security Hardening

Never:            Run as root. Bake secrets into images. Expose the docker
                  socket (/var/run/docker.sock) to app containers. Use :latest.
Always:           USER in Dockerfile. --read-only where possible. Resource
                  limits. Signed images (cosign), scanned (trivy). Private
                  registry + pull secrets. seccomp/apparmor defaults. Drop
                  capabilities: --cap-drop ALL --cap-add NET_BIND_SERVICE.

scan as early as CI:    trivy image myapp:1.0
secrets at runtime:     docker secret create db_pass ./pass.txt  (swarm)
                        or --env-file from a mounted secret file (compose)
daemon config:          limit exposure: hosts = [unix:///var/run/docker.sock]
lock the socket:        restrict to root group; never -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock in an app

13. Troubleshooting Cookbook

SymptomCheckUsual cause
Container exits immediatelydocker logs x; docker inspect -f \u0027{{.State.ExitCode}}\u0027 xApp crash, wrong CMD, missing env
Restart looplogs + exit code; healthcheck outputMissing dependency (db not ready), bad config
Port already allocateddocker ps -a + netstat -ano / ss -tulpnOld container still bound; host process on the port
Cannot reach service by namedocker network inspect; docker exec x getent hosts dbDifferent networks, or default bridge (no DNS)
Permission denied writing volumedocker exec x id; ls -l on host pathUID mismatch - match user in Dockerfile to host owner
Disk fulldocker system df -vLog driver never rotated; build cache; dangling images
Build picks stale codedocker history; .dockerignoreCOPY . . cached, or .git/venv in context
Slow I/Obind mount vs named volume; docker statsWindows/macOS bind mounts across OS boundary
Daemon will not startjournalctl -u docker -eCorrupt json daemon config, storage driver clash, full disk

14. Learning vs Production

AspectWhile learningIn production
Imageslatest on Docker HubPinned tags + digests, signed, scanned in CI
ComposeOne file on a laptopCompose files in git; real deployments on orchestrators
StateAnonymous volumesExternal managed databases; volumes backed up and restore-tested
NetworksDefault bridge, -p everywhereUser-defined networks, internal-only where possible, mesh/ingress in front
Cleanupdocker system prune -a blindlyLog rotation policies, registry GC, disk alerts on the daemon
RootEverything as rootNon-root USER, read-only rootfs, dropped caps, no docker.sock

15. Key Takeaways

  • Image = layered recipe, container = running meal; volumes carry data, networks carry names.
  • Order Dockerfile steps for cache: deps before source, and multi-stage keeps the final image slim.
  • User-defined networks give built-in DNS - containers connect by name.
  • Compose: depends_on needs service_healthy; down -v deletes data; config validates your YAML.
  • Prune in safety order and always read system df -v first.
  • Non-root, pinned digests, scanned and signed images are the production baseline.

Exercise: dockerize a small app you own: multi-stage Dockerfile, non-root user, healthcheck, named volume for its data, two services in compose with a health-gated depends_on - then break each piece on purpose and fix it with the cookbook.
